sentences.text: The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C) has been filed by the petitioners praying for quashing of FIR bearing No. 341/2018, registered at Police Station Mehrauli, New Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/506/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Mr. Naresh Kumar Chahar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
3. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Ms. Promila Rana and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Kamputer Singh from Police Station Mehrauli, Delhi.
This is a digitally signed order.

The brief facts of the present case are that petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 got married on 18.04.2016 at New Delhi as per Hindu rites and customs and out of said wedlock one male child was born.

On the complaint of respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing no. 341/2018 was registered at Police Station Mehrauli, New Delhi, for the offences punishable under Section 498A/506/406/34 of IPC Ravi Lakra & Ors vs State Of Delhi Nct & Anr on 31 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75629916/
1 against the petitioners.

entities.text: IPC Ravi Lakra & Ors vs State Of Delhi Nct & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is stated that the matter has been amicably settled between the parties vide Deed of Settlement / MOU dated 05.09.2019.
5.

On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent No.2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties vide Deed of Settlement / MOU dated 05.09.2019 and learned counsel for the petitioners submitted affidavit showing the protection of interest of minor child as per the judgment titled as Ganesh vs. Sudhirkumar Shrivastava, (2020) 20 SCC 787 passed by the Honble Supreme Court and the same is on record.
6.

It is submitted that respondent no.2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner No.1 and other family members.
7. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the full and final settled amount from petitioners and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
8. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will and without any coercion and also This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity
of the order
can be re-
verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 08/10/2023 at 07:29:39 the fact that the present matter is a family matter, I am of the opinion that no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
Moreover, there is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

9. Accordingly, FIR bearing No. 341/2018, registered at Police Station Mehrauli, New Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/506/406/34 of the IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
10. The present petition stands disposed of.
11. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J MAY 31, 2023/kss
